antithesis

an-TITH-uh-siss (stress on the second syllable) -- Greek anti- ('against') plus thesis ('a placing'): one idea placed directly against another. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Antithesis is a thing in direct contrast to another.

Careful, patient research is the antithesis of a wild guess.

Example

One restaurant on the block serves nine tiny courses on white tablecloths for two hundred dollars; the diner directly across the street -- three eggs and toast for four dollars, coffee poured before you sit down -- is its antithesis.

Two things set against each other point for point are antitheses. Unlike 'difference,' which can be small or partial, an antithesis is the full opposite.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

opposite: Opposite is the plain, everyday word for a thing completely reversed from another -- up is the opposite of down. Antithesis means the same total reversal but sounds formal and bookish, and it is saved for ideas, styles, and personalities: careful research is the antithesis of a wild guess.

reverse: The reverse is the exact turning-around of something -- run a sequence backward and you have its reverse. It stays close to directions, orders, and positions, while an antithesis sets whole ideas, characters, or styles against each other; a rival philosophy is an antithesis, not a reverse.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

match: a thing exactly like another

likeness: a close resemblance between two things

Where it sits · how completely the two things differ

contrast → antithesis → contradiction

contrast vs. antithesis: Contrast is weaker and more flexible than antithesis -- two shades of blue can be a contrast, while an antithesis is the total opposite, with nothing in between.

contradiction vs. antithesis: Contradiction pushes past antithesis: an antithesis sets two things against each other point for point, while a contradiction means the two cannot both be true at once -- one of them has to give.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — anti-: against, opposite (Greek)

root — -thesis: a placing, a setting down (Greek (tithenai, 'to place'))

Put it together: Greek antithesis meant 'a setting against,' from anti- ('against') and tithenai ('to place') -- an antithesis is one thing placed directly against another, from the same root that gives us thesis and hypothesis.

Use the root in a new word: hypothesis: After the second trial, Maya refused to abandon her hypothesis.

Root Check

Word Choice

Antithesis is almost always followed by 'of' -- 'the antithesis of kindness,' 'the antithesis of everything he stood for.' The plural is antitheses, and the matching adjective is antithetical.
